title: Adaptive head-slicing kernel prober for stable v2/v3 FlashAttention integration
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem:
We observe intermittent tail-latency regressions and cost increases when switching between FlashAttention v2 and v3 variants across different model shapes (variable head counts, sequence lengths) and GPU types. Current kernel selector chooses based on static heuristics (seq_len, dtype) and global benchmarks; this misses per-request shape mismatches and multi-tenant memory fragmentation that cause sudden kernel fallbacks or OOMs during decode.

Goal:
Build a lightweight runtime "kernel prober" that: (1) dynamically evaluates per-model/per-device head-slicing kernel candidates (including head-sliced variants for FAv2/FAv3), (2) maintains an LRU-based probe cache keyed by model signature + device topology, and (3) drives a conservative rollout of better kernels with telemetry and safe fallbacks to avoid regressions. Primary goals are reduced p99/p99.9 latency spikes, improved throughput for common real-world head/seq distributions, and safer v3 adoption.

Design summary:
- Head-slicing: implement an optional kernel variant that splits multi-head attention into smaller contiguous head blocks (e.g., 8->2x4) to reduce workspace and improve memory locality for certain FAv3 kernels. This is a low-level execution path that reorders attention dims before kernel invocation, with minimal graph changes.
- Prober: on first warmup for a (model,device,layout) signature, run a 3-sample microbenchmark across candidate kernels: native FAv2, FAv3-default, FAv3-head-sliced(N), and a fallback baseline. Each sample is short (1-3 tokens decode + prefill-mock) to minimize customer impact. Scores collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, workspace bytes, ephemeral allocation count.
- Scoring & policy: use a weighted score that favors tail latency and memory safety. Only promote a candidate if score improves tail latency by >= 5% without increasing memory allocations or causing allocation failures in probe. A promotion is applied to routing table for that signature for a TTL (default 48h) and logged.
- Safety: probes run on a small fraction of early requests (configurable 0.5% by default) and are rate-limited per-host and per-model. If a promoted kernel subsequently increases error rate or p99 by >10% for 1 minute, automatic rollback occurs.
- Instrumentation: new metrics (attn.kernel.probe.count, attn.kernel.promotion.count, attn.kernel.rollback.count, attn.kernel.signature.score_delta) and tags (model, device_family, candidate). Traces will include probe payloads for offline analysis.

Implementation plan:
1) Microbench harness (week 1): instrument a low-overhead harness in the runtime to run short encode/decode snippets under the same memory pool as normal requests.
2) Head-slicing shim (week 1-2): implement in C++ runtime a minimal reordering path that produces head-blocked buffers for kernel input without changing model graphs.
3) Prober logic & scoring (week 2): implement probe cadence, scoring, TTLs and safe promotion APIs.
4) Canary & e2e tests (week 3): unit tests, integration tests with multi-tenant mixture profiles, and a canary rollout on dedicated capacity with synthetic traffic.
5) Gradual rollout (week 4): enable on <1% production traffic, monitor, then 5%, then 20% if all metrics green.

Rollout/Canary criteria:
- No increase in decode error rates or OOMs during canary windows.
- p99 tail latency decrease or no change; target: p99 <= baseline * 1.00 and p95 reduced by at least 3% for promoted signatures.
- Observability events for every promotion/rollback with linked trace and per-request sample.

Rollback/Contingency:
- Immediate un-promotion via control-plane flag and revert TTL to previous kernel.
- If regressions are systemic across devices, disable head-slicing globally and trigger ENG investigation.

Documentation & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Adaptive+Head-Slicing+Kernel+Prober
- RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/198
- Microbench harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/eng/attn-prober
comments: 2025-11-03: Kickoff meeting – aligned on lightweight probes, head-slicing as reversible shim. Action: Lucas to draft microbench harness and Maya to prototype head reorder kernel.

2025-11-04: PoC microbench done. Early numbers on c6i-gpu (A100) show head-sliced FAv3 reduces p95 by 8% for 12-head transformers at seq=512, but increases p50 slightly (+2%). Logged traces: gh-PR-1210.
2025-11-05: Discovered memory fragmentation when running probes concurrently with heavy prefill; added probe host-rate limit. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2215
2025-11-06: Security review waived for initial probe (no customer data persisted); flagged for ops review for multi-tenant safety. Ops request: telemetry retention for probe traces = 7 days.

2025-11-07: Integration test with dedicated pool (3 nodes) found a corner-case where head-sliced path caused alignment mismatch on older cuBLAS builds; workaround added to detect cuBLAS version before promoting. Issue filed: ENG-20376.
2025-11-08: Currently wiring promotion/rollback metrics into Console dashboards. Next: schedule canary for 0.5% traffic next Tuesday (2025-11-11).
